measurement: R1 (理 11217) — paired per-problem bootstrap, 95% CI on the DIFFERENCE, plus exact McNemar on success. Replaces every point delta in the transfer table.
why_paired: each pair is the SAME problems run twice; the arms differ only in whether the head acts at the post-inspect decision. An unpaired interval ignores that and is wider than the data warrants. McNemar uses only the DISCORDANT pairs, which is where the whole effect lives -- the agreement group moves -1 of 121.

pairs.pair: seed21 head -> seed21 slice 4 (SAME generator run)

pairs.mcnemar: base-only 5 · G-only 14 · p = 0.064  <- NOT significant at .05

what_survives_the_intervals: all five G-vs-base pairs exclude zero on BOTH limbs. The two 300-problem pairs are unambiguous (p < 1e-4, success CI [+7.7,+18.3] and [+6.3,+16.3]). The effect is not a point estimate artefact.
TWO_TESTS_DISAGREE_ON_ONE_PAIR_AND_I_AM_: seed21-ORIGINAL-head -> seed47: the bootstrap CI is [+1.3, +22.7], which excludes zero, while McNemar gives p = 0.064, which does not clear .05. Nineteen discordant pairs is thin. The two tests are answering slightly different questions -- the bootstrap resamples problems, McNemar conditions on the discordant set -- and at n=75 that gap is visible. The honest reading of THAT pair alone is 'consistent with the others, not independently significant'; the 300-problem pairs are what carries.
P9_b_now_has_an_interval_rather_than_a_j: success -4.0 [-9.3, +0.0] and actions +0.11 [-0.04, +0.27] -- both include zero, McNemar p = 0.25. My 'FAIL by the letter, NULL by size' reading is now backed by an interval instead of by my own eye.
bounds: 10,000 bootstrap resamples, seed 11, resampling PROBLEMS (the unit of independence).
McNemar exact two-sided on the discordant pairs; no continuity correction, no asymptotic approximation, because several cells are small.
Six pairs tested with no multiplicity adjustment. The two 300-problem pairs survive any reasonable correction; the n=75 pairs would not all survive one.
